name: Dennis Johnson
summary: All-Defensive First Team 1979 and 1980; anchor of league-best Sonics defense; called basketball's top defensive guard.

name: Neil Johnston
summary: Known for hook-shot scoring and rebounding; no written evaluation of his defense found; inferred average.

name: Eddie Jones
summary: Active, long-armed wing who drew 2+ steals per game early; All-Defensive honors came slightly later (1998-2000).

name: Ed Macauley
summary: Slender, undersized scoring center; Celtics' post defense was considered the team's weakness until Russell.

name: Sidney Moncrief
summary: Won the first DPOY in 1983 and was All-Defensive First Team 1983; widely seen as the premier defensive guard.

name: Paul Pressey
summary: All-Defensive First Team 1985 and 1986; described as a lockdown defender on Nelson's Bucks.

name: Dan Roundfield
summary: All-Defensive First Team 1980 and Second Team 1981; called the defensive backbone of Fratello-era Hawks frontcourt.

name: Dolph Schayes
summary: Celebrated competitor and rebounder, but sources focus on scoring; no clear assessment of his defense.

name: Phil Smith
summary: All-Defensive Second Team 1976 alongside All-NBA Second Team.

name: Andrew Toney
summary: Feared scorer; coverage is all about his offense, and his defense was generally viewed as a weakness.

name: Jack Twyman
summary: Described almost entirely as a pure shooter/scorer; no defensive praise found.

name: Norm Van Lier
summary: All-Defensive First Team 1976 and 1977 (Second 1975); full-court pressure 'doberman' with Sloan.

name: Gus Williams
summary: Quick ballhawk with a solid defensive reputation, top-10 in steals yearly, key to the Sonics' league-best defense.

name: Dave Bing
summary: Known as an all-around scorer and leader; no defensive honors or notes either way.

name: Maurice Cheeks
summary: All-Defensive First Team 1983-86; elite steals and pressure defense; among Sixers' best defenders ever.

name: Terry Dischinger
summary: Efficient scoring forward; no written defensive assessment found.

name: Clyde Lovellette
summary: Physical, rough offensive center who pulled bigs outside; not known for defense.

name: George McGinnis
summary: Powerful, high-steal forward but criticized as undisciplined; no defensive honors.

name: Jeff Ruland
summary: Physical 'Beef Brother' who boxed out and fronted opponents; slow footed, not a shot blocker.

name: Otis Birdsong
summary: Scoring guard; no defensive honors or commentary found.

name: Gail Goodrich
summary: Small 6-1 scorer whose height was noted as a handicap; West covered tougher assignments.

name: Bill Laimbeer
summary: Strong positional rebounder and intimidating physical presence, but limited mobility and shot blocking.

name: Fat Lever
summary: All-Defensive Second Team 1988; Nuggets' career steals leader; tough ballhawk.

name: Michael Ray Richardson
summary: All-Defensive First Team 1980 and 1981; led league in steals.

name: Nate Thurmond
summary: Renowned defensive center; All-Defensive Second Team 1973 and 1974; considered among the toughest defenders of Kareem.

name: Tom Chambers
summary: Offense-first scoring forward; defense rarely mentioned and generally viewed as indifferent.

name: Ron Harper
summary: Athletic, long guard averaging 2+ steals; strong defensive tools before his 1990 knee injury.

name: Kenny Sears
summary: Scoring/rebounding forward; no defensive commentary found.

name: Rod Strickland
summary: Creative playmaker; coverage centers on offense and conflicts with Carlesimo; defense not regarded as a strength.

name: Archie Clark
summary: Primarily a one-on-one scorer; SI noted sharp defense on Goodrich in one 1973 game.
